subject: ventures/ghost-members-export-analyzer
professional: a newsletter operator / email-deliverability lead who runs a paid Ghost publication and cleans member lists

evidence.correctness: Ran the real calc.mjs (analyze) on a 300-row Ghost-style export generated in the scratchpad (random labels, tiers, comp, unsubscribed, deleted rows, sent 0/3/9/10/11/25/40) and diffed against a separate Python csv-module implementation written from the page's stated rules: live/paid/comp/free/removed 285/36/7/242/15, MRR 288, processing 19.152 (36x8x2.9% + 36x0.30), conversion 36/278 = 0.1295, judged 154, bands never/low/mid/high 61/16/44/33, quiet 39, unsubscribed-free 28, prospects 25, four label rows and all 12 growth months: every value identical. Two edge probes found model/wording departures: a member exactly 90 days old is not 'quiet' although the page says 'at least this many days' (strict > in code); a bare open-rate of 0.5 is read as 50% but 1 as 1%. Not capped at 2 because outputs were recomputed, but held at 3 not 4 because the input layout is from memory, never checked against a real Ghost export.
evidence.completeness: Every README feature is present and populated on the 500-row example and my 300-row file: paid/free/comp, conversion, engagement bands, quiet and unsubscribed counts with savings, label table with small-group marking, paid-by-tier, growth and removals by month, engaged prospects, growth CSV download, Load example, Clear, date-format detection. No stubs or TODOs. Gap: the README says what the quiet members are but the tool outputs only a count; emails are dropped at parse so the publisher cannot get the list to act on.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject: 27 pass, 0 fail, about 0.19 s. Hand-seeded 7 mutations in calc.mjs, reverted each with git checkout (git status clean afterwards, 27 pass again): only 2 caught (dropping the fixed processing fee; letting comp count as paid). 5 survived with all 27 tests green: engaged threshold 0.6 -> 0.7, quiet age > -> >=, minSends >= -> >, prospect threshold 0.6 -> 0.5, and conversion denominator excluding comp -> including comp (the stated 'comp never in conversion' rule has no test with a comp member). Every user-visible threshold is untested at its boundary. page.test.mjs is mostly string greps of the HTML, which fits a disclaimer check but proves nothing about numbers.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (317 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, usage.test.mjs and the index.html script. Pure functions, no DOM, small module, clean aliasing, delimiter/BOM/UTF-16/day-first date handling, HTML-escaped output, localStorage guarded, opt-out and DNT honoured. Defects: a negative email_count is accepted (sent -5 is stored); a bare open-rate of 1 is read as 1% but 0.5 as 50%; the sample-data generator ships inside the production calc.mjs; delimiter detection counts separators inside quoted fields; the quiet filter treats a member with no parseable signup date as old enough to flag.
evidence.claims: Checked the privacy claims (no network calls, usage counters local only, emails and names not kept), the disclaimer and independence text, the 'matched by alias from memory, no real export available' admission (present on the page, README and VENTURE.yaml - honest), the 27-test claim, MIN_GROUP of 5, bands and thresholds as written on the page, and llms.txt (github.io host is the pre-deploy source URL that build_pages_site.py rewrites; not a served defect). Weakness: the page and README sell 'free-to-paid conversion' when the figure is the current share of non-comp members with a Stripe id or tier (no cohort, and churned payers with an old Stripe id still count; the model list admits the Stripe-id caveat). The statement in VENTURE.yaml that no Admin screen ranks inactive members is unverified.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a Ghost publisher exports members, drops the CSV, sees paid/free/comp, never-opened share and an estimated saving. The headline job, deciding whom to re-engage or remove, ends at a count: the tool deliberately discards emails and offers no download of the quiet list or a Ghost filter recipe (e.g. open count 0 and created before date), so the publisher must redo the selection in Ghost Admin. The 'paid' flag over-counts anyone whose subscription ended but whose Stripe id remains, and the example is the only data the tool has ever read; the real export layout is unconfirmed. Good: assumptions are typed, tables are scrollable, runs on a phone.
evidence.domain: A newsletter operator / email deliverability practitioner would check: are opens trustworthy, is the removal advice staged, are costs real. The page stages removal (send a re-engagement email first) and warns that blocked tracking undercounts opens, which is right. It does not mention Apple Mail Privacy Protection, which inflates opens automatically since 2021 and so overstates the 'engaged' and prospect pool; 60% as 'engaged' and the 20/60 band cuts are uncited. 'Conversion' is an end-state paid share, not a funnel conversion, and the 5 to 10% benchmark is hedged but unsourced. Savings multiply flagged members by the typed per-1000 rate and linear per-member plan cost, which the page admits may not match Ghost(Pro) tier pricing.

defects.what: Seeded mutations in core thresholds go undetected: 5 of 7 (engaged cutoff, quiet age comparison, minSends comparison, prospect cutoff, conversion denominator counting comp) leave all 27 tests green; no test has a comp member in the conversion case or checks any threshold at its boundary
The headline job (who to re-engage or remove) ends in a count: emails are discarded at parse and there is no download or filter recipe for the quiet free members, so the user cannot act on the result
Quiet-member age uses strict > while the page says 'joined at least this many days ago' (a member exactly N days old is not flagged)
'Free-to-paid conversion' is the current share of non-comp members holding a Stripe id or tier; former payers with a lingering Stripe id count as paid and the label overstates what is measured
Open-based engagement bands and prospects ignore Apple Mail Privacy Protection auto-opens, which inflate opens; page only warns about undercounting; band cutoffs are uncited
Column names and value wording are from memory; never read a real Ghost export (disclosed); bare open-rate 1 vs 0.5 is read as 1% vs 50%; negative email_count accepted
The sample-data generator (sampleCsv) ships inside the production calc.mjs and the parser counts delimiters inside quoted fields; a quiet filter accepts undated members as old enough

verdict: The arithmetic is right: every count, band, label row, growth month and money figure matched an independent Python recomputation on a 300-row Ghost-style export, the privacy and disclaimer claims are backed by files, and the page candidly says the column names are from memory. It does not meet the bar because verification scores 1: five of seven seeded threshold mutations (engaged cutoff, quiet age and minSends comparisons, prospect cutoff, and counting comp members in the conversion denominator) left all 27 tests green, so the rules that decide who is flagged are protected only by the two happy-path cases. Fitness and domain are 2: the tool tells a publisher how many members look removable but discards the list, labels a paid-share as conversion, and treats opens as trustworthy without noting Apple Mail Privacy Protection. Worst defect: untested core thresholds (medium), with the missing quiet-member export the biggest product gap.
